label: early original-phase q/a/e/w/o/c after an h/r/2-type prefix
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at steps t=2..6 (mass mostly at t=3-4), never at t<2, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. The current input is almost always one of q, a, e, w (about 78% of mass), then o, c, 0, with d/m rare; other tokens essentially never. Usually the first occurrence of that token (97% of mass). Whether it fires is strongly modulated by the preceding prefix: firing is boosted when earlier inputs (first token, prev2, prev) come from a set like h, r, 2, l, p, k, 3, i, s, m. The strongest activations (e.g. h 2 2 r [e], h i r r [q], 2 r r r [q]) have prefixes made up entirely of these tokens. The same q/a/e/w tokens after other prefixes mostly do not fire, which is the main source of false positives; this looks like a graded sum over the prefix rather than a crisp rule. Misses include repeated tokens (a a), some d/0 inputs, and step-5 activations.
